summary: South Carolina's bathroom restriction now reaches higher education. House Bill 4756, signed by Governor Henry McMaster on 15 May 2026, requires transgender students in public schools, colleges and universities to use restrooms matching their sex assigned at birth; the Senate amended the bill before passage. The ACLU of South Carolina, responding on 18 May 2026, describes it as discrimination against transgender students in both K-12 and higher education. A July 2026 risk assessment records the expansion to universities as adding campus settings to a pre-existing restriction and places South Carolina among jurisdictions with escalating law rather than in the harshest tier.
tangentialFactors:
South Carolina is one of four states operating a freeze-frame policy on prison treatments for transgender inmates, alongside Tennessee, Arkansas and Utah.

It is the only state whose domestic violence statutes cover only opposite-sex couples.

Enforcement of the bathroom law is unsettled in one respect. On 10 September 2025 the U.S. Supreme Court denied South Carolina's 26 August 2025 request to pause a Fourth Circuit order requiring a school district to let transgender student John Doe use the boys' bathroom while his equal-protection and federal education anti-discrimination challenge proceeds. The law is unenforceable against him during the litigation, and the courts have not ruled on its merits.
localsOnly:
The governor signed a ban on transgender participation in sports on 17 May 2022.

Budget appropriations for 2024-25 and 2025-26 require students to use bathrooms based on sex at the time of birth.

On 11 March 2020 the U.S. District Court for the District of South Carolina, in Gender and Sexuality Alliance v. Spearman, struck down S.C. Code § 59-32-30(A)(5), the 1988 provision barring discussion of same-sex relationships in public-school health education except in the context of sexually transmitted diseases, holding it unconstitutional under the Fourteenth Amendment Equal Protection Clause and barring its enforcement.

In April 2016 Governor Nikki Haley said she opposed a transgender bathroom-restriction bill then before the Legislature and considered it unnecessary.

Local employment protections covering gender identity exist in Mount Pleasant, Myrtle Beach and Richland County, and for city employees in Columbia, Charleston and Latta.
outOfScopeNotes:
No South Carolina case or ruling is recorded on cell placement, special units, or solitary or segregation for transgender prisoners.

South Carolina has enacted no hate-crime statute; the earliest sourced confirmation of that absence is dated 26 March 2007.

The sodomy provision remains unrepealed.
